observations: Iron-bound crates appear in a safe 2x2x2 cube right after the super body slam unlock, then as a column under a 1UP beside a Nitro.
15 Nitros and 1 TNT are mostly mixed into ordinary groups rather than standing alone.
Nitros sit next to frogs and a berserker, so the fight pushes the player toward the explosive.
Masks precede hazards: S1-d before the Nitro mixes, S3-d before the ? on TNT.
Three slot crates act as timers; one is explicitly coupled to the iron column.
Density: S1 31, S2 17, S3 8, S4 a 10-crate reward block then a 10-Nitro gauntlet.
8 of 15 Nitros sit in the last two clusters: the biggest count trap is at the exit.
Stacks are uniform 2- and 3-stacks; complexity comes from neighbours, not shapes.
Bonus: striped sandwiches, arrow-to-floating-crate twice, outline exit with a pit crate before the switch.
badgeConvention: ttBadges: red 1 / blue 2 / green 3 = time-stop crate seconds in time trial; A = crate that is an Aku crate in time trial. Drawn icon = normal-mode type. Key 'wood?' = a counted crate whose type cannot be read (gutter blur or hidden behind a badge)
countingRule: F3 cumulative counts include the checkpoint crate; 'NN (MM)' = without (with) Nitro. After the green ! all 15 Nitro count. Steel arrows, steel ! and the green ! are listed under 'uncounted'. Bonus: only 4 of 10 outline icons are counted boxes (header x18); the other 6 are listed as uncounted 'outlineFooting'.

geometryObservations: A walking stage: the main course has no full-width chasm until the hole near the goal (G-S4-d). Its gaps are shallow water bands (G-S1-a, G-S1-c, G-S2-b, G-S3-b, G-S4-a/b/c) and holes that take only part of the width (G-S1-b, G-S3-a, G-S3-c), so difficulty comes from enemies and hidden explosives, not from jumping.

Three lanes by construction: the low stone walls on both edges are walkable (F3 p012L), and the guide uses them as the answer to almost every threat — wizard beams (TA4), the frog beside a Nitro (mask hint 7), the berserker blockade (mask hint 8 uses the right side) — while big rocks and holes end the wall lanes at chosen points (O-S1-a, G-S1-b, G-S2-a).

The new enemy (wizard) debuts right after a hole (G-S1-b → E-S1-c), and each later wizard is paired with a different space: above a narrow passage behind a berserker (E-S2-c/d), and beyond a tunnel with a slot crate timing out (E-S3-d).

Known enemies from stage 1 (frogs, goats, berserkers) are recombined with explosives: frog + Nitro twice (E-S1-b, E-S4-a), berserker + Nitro lane (E-S3-a + O-S3-a), berserker pair before the green ! and a berserker in front of the Nitro gate (E-S4-c, E-S4-f).
Water is the frog habitat: four of five frog records stand in or at a water band, so a purple band on screen reads as "a hopper will cut across here" before the frog is visible.

Chokes hold exactly one enemy each — the S2 stepped passage (berserker), the S3 castle arch (goat), the goal gate (berserker) — so a choke always means a forced engagement or a timed pass, never a free walk.
The S3 lane squeeze (P-S3-b) is a three-option test: water (safe but where the frogs come from), sword (timed), Nitro (lethal); the guide's solution is a timed jump past the enemy rather than a lane.

Enemy density stays level (5, 5, 4, 7 enemies per section) while crate density falls (31, 17, 8, 11 boxes): the late sections are combat-led, and the reward block sits on the calm slope right after C3 (P-S4-a) as the last rest.

The final stretch stacks one blocker per beat: blockade → hole → bridge → green ! with Nitros → berserker in the gate → Nitro columns around the portal. Escalation at the exit is done with blockers, not with longer gaps.
The only long jump (G-S4-d) comes last and is set up by a run-up from a rock; everything else is a hop (log, wall, step).

The time-trial line is the walls plus diagonal cuts (TT 02, 15–17, 26–27): the course is built so the shortest-looking line is not the fastest (F3 p103R intro) — useful geometry for a skate line, which also wants raised edges.

The bonus is the stage's jump room: three walkways with 1–2 u gaps, steel arrows as the vertical tool, and a pit under an outline staircase whose crate must be taken before the switch fills the space (G-B-c).
geometryTransfer: Walkable curbs as skate lanes: line a 5–7 m path with 1-crate-high (≈1.15 m), ≈1 m-wide walls; ordinary platform edges already grind, so a rider at 12 m/s cruise gets two grind lanes that bypass floor enemies. End each wall run with a `rock` or a `pit` notch every 15–25 m so the player has to drop to the floor where you want them (the Gee Wiz rock/hole rhythm).

Projectile enemy after a hole: a `sentry` 6–10 m past a 2–2.5 m `pit` notch (well inside the 5.6 m running jump) so the player lands into its fire; give the projectile a slow speed and let a spin destroy it (wizard beam), and keep the wall lane beside it as the safe answer.

Three-lane squeeze: on a 5 m path put soft ground (`groundSpeedLimit`, e.g. 2.4 m/s) on the left 1.7 m, a `spinner` in the centre, a Nitro on the right; the intended counter is a timed full jump over the centre enemy (2.85 m apex) or a charged ollie (1.7 m) — check the enemy hitbox height against the ollie before relying on it.
Blockade choke: two `charger`s or `spinner`s side by side across a 5 m path, leaving one 1.2–1.5 m gap on one side; on the board the gap is a line choice at cruise speed, on foot a timed run past.

End-of-level long jump: a 3–4 m `pit` across the full width with a rock as the run-up marker and a 2.3 m-wide bridge as the landing, placed after the last checkpoint; on foot it is a real jump (5.6 m reach), on the board an easy ollie (≈6.6 m at cruise), so it rewards skaters without blocking walkers.

Bonus jump room: three 6–8 m walkways with 1.2–2.3 m gaps, a steel arrow under a floating block on each, and a pit under an outline staircase with one crate low in the pit that must be taken before the `bang` materialises the stairs.
